t.E960.agn: In 2010 EFSA set the acceptable daily intake (ADI) at 4 mg/kg body weight, expressed as steviol; in 2024 it found insufficient grounds to raise this limit. EFSA reported that this limit may be exceeded in high-consuming adults and children, the main source being soft drinks.
t.E960.body: Steviol glycosides are broken down in the body by the same pathways, and their common breakdown product is steviol.
t.E960.eff.0.t: The daily limit may be exceeded; the main source is soft drinks
t.E960.prod: May be produced by extraction from stevia leaves, by enzymatic conversion or by fermentation.
t.E960.pw.0: According to EFSA, the daily intake limit may be exceeded in high-consuming children, especially young children; the main source is drinks.
t.E960.regx.0: Safety assessment; ADI set at 4 mg/kg (as steviol).
t.E960.regx.1: Added to the EU list as a sweetener (Regulation (EU) 1131/2011).
t.E960.regx.2: The name E 960 changed to E 960a (from Stevia); enzymatically produced E 960c added (Regulation (EU) 2021/1156).
t.E960.regx.3: Glucosylated steviol glycosides added as E 960d (Regulation (EU) 2023/447).
t.E960.regx.5: Insufficient grounds found to raise the ADI; 4 mg/kg maintained.
t.E960.summary: A calorie-free sweetener purified from the leaves of the stevia plant. Used in drinks, yoghurt and sugar-free products.
t.E960.what: Intense sweeteners obtained from the leaves of the stevia plant (or produced by enzymes or fermentation); listed in the EU under the sub-numbers E 960a–E 960d.
